rounds.text: Aurique Ltd is demonstrating a powerful operational and profit turnaround that the market has yet to fully appreciate [E44]. Compounded profit growth has accelerated impressively, reaching 23% over 3 years and surging by 65% over the trailing twelve months [E15, E16], backed by explicit screen signals noting a net profit increase of 233% year-over-year [E39]. This bottom-line momentum is reinforced by superior efficiency, featuring a remarkable Return on Assets of 106.96% that vastly outperforms the sector benchmark of 4.92% [E7]. Insider conviction strongly validates this fundamental recovery, as promoter shareholding has increased substantially by 20.28 percentage points to reach 73.08% [E29]. Furthermore, the company benefits from operating within an FMCG sector tailwind with a score of +0.54, providing a supportive macro backdrop for its setup [E43]. Conceded: [E13], [E26], [E37].

Aurique Ltd carries severe fundamental risks that are entirely disconnected from its elevated share price, which currently sits at 100% of its 52-week range [E4]. The company is suffering from a catastrophic collapse in top-line performance, evidenced by a compounded sales growth of -77% over 5 years, -89% over 3 years, and -84% over the trailing twelve months [E11, E12, E13]. Operational execution is deeply impaired, featuring a yearly operating-margin trend that has been decreasing over the last 9 years, hitting an extreme -2840% in Mar 2018 [E20, E21]. Financial stability is severely compromised by a current ratio of just 0.12x, where current liabilities vastly exceed current assets, alongside high borrowings of Rs 28.68 Cr and a flagged low interest coverage ratio [E26, E27, E34]. Furthermore, the business generates negative cash flows—including operating cash flow of Rs -3.76 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -2.94 Cr—while being burdened by massive high debtors of 1,862 days and contingent liabilities of Rs 18.1 Cr [E24, E25, E36, E37]. Valuation metrics are heavily strained, with an EV/EBITDA of 15.93x exceeding the sector benchmark of 10.62x, and a deeply negative book value yielding a price-to-book ratio of -17.64x [E1, E10]. conceded: [E16]

The bear points to a collapse in multi-year sales growth [E11, E12, E13], but ignores that shorter-term profitability is sharply accelerating, featuring a 65% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and a dramatic 233% year-on-year net profit surge [E16, E39]. The bear highlights distressed operating margins [E20, E21], but fails to account for a stellar return on assets of 106.96%, which vastly outperforms the sector benchmark of 4.92% [E7]. While the bear cites severe cash flow deficits and debt burdens [E24, E25, E27], insiders are aggressively backing the turnaround, with promoter holdings jumping by over 20 percentage points from 52.80% to 73.08% [E29]. Furthermore, the business is benefiting from a supportive macro environment with the FMCG sector firmly in a tailwind [E43, E45], while recent operational metrics show profitability growing both year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter [E40, E41]. conceded: [E11], [E20], [E27], [E36], [E37].

The bull’s reliance on short-term profit growth [E16, E39] ignores the fundamental reality that the company’s core business is in a state of terminal decline, evidenced by compounded sales growth that has cratered by 84% to 89% over the last three years [E12, E13]. While the bull cites a high ROA [E7], this figure is disconnected from the company’s actual liquidity crisis, where current liabilities vastly exceed current assets with a current ratio of only 0.12x [E26]. The claim that the turnaround is supported by promoter buying [E29] fails to mitigate the severe operational risks, specifically the unsustainable debtor cycle of 1,862 days [E37] and the massive contingent liabilities of Rs 18.1 Cr [E36]. Furthermore, the bull’s optimism regarding profitability is undermined by the fact that the company’s operating cash flow was negative [E24] and free cash flow was negative [E25] in the most recent reporting period. The stock’s valuation is also highly precarious, as it trades at an EV/EBITDA of 15.93x, which is significantly more expensive than the sector benchmark of 10.62x [E10]. Conceded: [E16], [E29], [E43].
